articles.title: ‘The Visit’ at Pasadena Playhouse Review: The ’50s Absurdist Comedy Is Too Smug in Its Peak-Bleak View of Venal Humanity, but Jefferson Mays and Melinda Page Hamilton Are Worth the Visit
articles.summary: When an “Amadeus” revival opened at Pasadena Playhouse in February, it was such a spectacular success on every level that you wouldn’t have minded if the keepers of the venerable San Gabriel Valley venue just turned over the keys to the place for a while to the two Tony winners most responsible for…
body: The show’s creepiest characters — no contest here — are a couple of aging, balding, blind eunuchs (played by Jake Levy and Lauren Worsham)who seem to be part of Claire’s entourage for no good reason, other than to figure into the tale of woe she eventually tells, which finally explains why they know their way around the town so well despite being sightless visitors. Their presence brings “The Visit” almost right up to the edge of horror, which is where thematically it kind of belongs, despite all the zingers, smirks and guffaws. The play seems to want to flirt with the idea of Grand Guignol, even if remains more firmly rooted in the land of Samuel Beckett.
“The Visit” runs through Oct. 4 at Pasadena Playhouse, located at 39 South El Molino Ave. in Pasadena. Phone: 626-356-7529. For tickets and more information, visit http://www.pasadenaplayhouse.org.

articles.title: Rolf de Heer Named President of Tokyo Film Festival Jury
articles.summary: The Tokyo International Film Festival has named Australian director Rolf de Heer president of the international competition jury for the festival’s 39th edition. De Heer has spent more than 40 years in Tasmania, Australia, directing, writing and producing films across a broad range of genres and…
body: “For any of us attending the Tokyo International Film Festival, it is a privilege,” de Heer said. “For me, as a filmmaker, it is even more so. The more films I manage to make, the fewer films I manage to see, especially on the big screen. But as a part of this jury, I have the duty, the obligation, to see at least 15 films and talk about them with other filmmakers.”

Hisamatsu Takeo, festival director of TIFF, said he was delighted to welcome de Heer as jury president. “With his distinctive perspective and unwavering commitment to filmmaking, de Heer has spent decades opening up new possibilities in cinema,” Hisamatsu said. “We look forward to the fresh dialogue and discoveries that his wealth of experience and deep insight will bring to this year’s Competition and its diverse selection of films.”

De Heer trained at the Australian Film, Television and Radio School and has since written or co-written 14 screenplays that reached the screen as feature films. His director’s credits run to 15 and a half features spanning a range of budgets and genres, and he has produced or co-produced 16 fiction films and five documentaries.

Discovery, first revealed the project during an investor call in 2025. Steven Spielberg is returning as executive producer alongside Maiden Voyage’s Eleanor Columbus.
body: Joe Dante’s original 1984 “Gremlins,” which played a role in creating the PG-13 film rating, was a horror comedy following a young boy named Billy who receives a cute, furry yet mysterious creature called a Mogwai. The two become fast friends, but Billy’s new pet comes with two strict rules: Never get the Mogwai wet and never feed it after midnight. Of course, those regulations are broken. The gremlin then multiplies and creates chaos in Billy’s small town during the holiday season.

The first “Gremlins” was a box office smash, grossing $212 million worldwide against a budget of about $11 million. The 1990 follow-up, “Gremlins 2: The New Batch,” only mustered $41 million by the end of its run but is considered a cult classic.

articles.title: Barry Diller Drops Bid to Acquire MGM Resorts: ‘We Didn’t Feel the Mix Was Coming Together’
articles.summary: People Inc., the media company controlled by Barry Diller, is scrapping its proposed bid to acquire MGM Resorts International. People Inc. (which changed its name from IAC this spring) owns about 27% of MGM Resorts.
body: Diller, who serves as People Inc.’s chairman and senior executive, said in a statement, “There are lots of ingredients that go into a proposal of this kind on its way to completion. We didn’t feel the mix was coming together in the way we had hoped and have decided not to pursue taking the company private at this time.”

Diller added, “What is undimmed is our belief in the future of MGM Resorts. We continue to hold 66.8 million shares representing approximately 27% of MGM Resorts and have total confidence in both the management and the Company’s prospects.”

The media mogul added, “People Incorporated is doing just fine with its principal publishing business achieving its 11th quarter of growth with plenty of cash to both invest in its business and purchase its stock.”
People Inc. remains “open to and interested in the possibility of a strategic transaction with MGM Resorts and look forward to considering a range of alternatives,” Diller said.

articles.title: ‘He made something every single day’: David Lynch’s inscrutable photography celebrated in LA show
articles.summary: The director’s surrealist films defined Los Angeles. Now the city is celebrating his other passion: photography. No one can bring Los Angeles together like David Lynch.
body: The first posthumous exhibition of the director and artist’s photographs went on display at LA’s Pace Gallery this weekend, drawing a massive crowd of goths, weirdos and art world observers to celebrate a creative mind that has few equals in American pop culture history.

Lynch’s disappearance from this mortal plane last year has not dimmed the public’s appreciation for his surrealist, idiosyncratic perspective on American life. The exhibition – featuring photos that are erotic, disturbing and sometimes comically violent – encapsulates all the things that made Lynch one of the city’s foremost creative minds.

Photos of mysterious women blowing smoke, multiple exposures of a nude subject on a chaise longue, dissected animals; the work is “radical”, said Bill Griffin, managing partner for Pace Gallery. “It dealt with the human condition in a very large way. It dealt with consciousness and unconsciousness.” Pace represented Lynch for years, and is spearheading the efforts to maintain and catalogue his fine art work with the David Lynch Foundation.

articles.title: Elizabeth Holmes to Be Moved From Prison to Halfway House in 2027
articles.summary: The disgraced Theranos founder will be placed in an Austin-area facility in August 2027 as she serves out her reduced sentence for defrauding investors.
body: Elizabeth Holmes, the imprisoned founder of Theranos who duped investors with a claim to have revolutionized blood testing and was sentenced to more than 11 years for fraud, will reportedly be moved from a Texas prison into a halfway house in 2027.

On Wednesday, ABC News reported that Holmes is scheduled to be placed in the Austin Transitional Center in Del Valle, Texas, on Aug. 23, 2027. The network cited an update from the Department of Justice’s Victim Notification System.

Known for her strikingly deep, husky baritone voice and uniform black wardrobe, Holmes was a Silicon Valley icon as the proprietary technology Theranos said it invented was primed to disrupt modern medicine. But a 2015 Wall Street Journal investigation found that Theranos’ proprietary technology was a ruse, and only a dozen of the hundreds of tests it offered were actually being performed. In fact, the company relied on third-party devices and traditional blood testing to perform what it said was its industry-shattering tech.
Following the company’s decline, Holmes went from Silicon Valley wunderkind to epitomize a “fake it ’til you make it” mentality that permeated the tech industry.

articles.title: ‘Milo’ Review: Marion Cotillard Carries a Somber, Classically Made French Drama with Hints of Film Noir
articles.summary: Théodore Pellerin also stars in the latest feature by 80-year-old actress turned director Nicole Garcia ('My American Uncle'), which premiered in competition at San Sebastián.
body: The struggling working-class character in that movie comes to mind when we first meet 40-something Alice (Cotillard), who arrives by bus in Romans-sur-Isère, a tough and not exactly picturesque rural enclave in southeastern France. Desperate for a job and a place to stay, Alice gets hired as a waitress at a local eatery that resembles a French Applebee’s, except it looks much more depressing, while holing up in a gloomy, barely-furnished apartment in the local housing projects.

It’s obvious from the start that Alice has an alternative agenda — the map she keeps tucked away in her bag gives this away — and her plans become increasingly clear when we see her spying on Milo (Pellerin), a 20-year-old auto mechanic and frequent client of the restaurant where she works.

articles.title: Boorman and the Devil review – enjoyable re-evaluation of the disaster that was Exorcist II: The Heretic
articles.summary: John Boorman generously details the mortifying experience of making a sequel to 1973 hit horror The Exorcist, which was widely and unfairly panned. David Kittredge gives us a thoroughly enjoyable, detailed account of the catastrophe that was John Boorman’s 1977 film Exorcist II: The Heretic, the…
body: According to an apocryphal tale gleefully repeated by William Friedkin, director of the first film, the sequel resulted in an enraged audience one night turning round and booing Warner Brothers executives in the back row of the cinema, and then chasing them out of the building and down the street. Boorman desperately recut the film with the sillier bits removed. But the damage was done.

Boorman is interviewed here and generously goes into great detail about his painful and mortifying experience with the film, how he had originally been offered the first Exorcist, disliked the story and turned it down, but was induced to take on the sequel. Perhaps Kittredge could have made it clearer how risky it was for Boorman to have taken on a project which he fundamentally didn’t believe in and was somehow creatively working against. He hired a kind of script-and-direction consultant, his friend Rospo Pallenberg, whose influence with Boorman annoyed the cast.
points: John Boorman generously details the mortifying experience of making a sequel to 1973 hit horror The Exorcist, which was widely and unfairly panned.

articles.title: Rolf de Heer Named Jury President for Tokyo Film Festival
articles.summary: The Australian filmmaker behind ‘Bad Boy Bubby,’ ‘Ten Canoes’ and ‘Charlie’s Country’ will preside over the international competition jury at TIFF’s 39th edition.
body: Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer will serve as president of the international competition jury at this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival.

“For any of us attending the Tokyo International Film Festival, it is a privilege. For me, as a filmmaker, it is even more so,” de Heer said in a statement. “The more films I manage to make, the fewer films I manage to see, especially on the big screen. But as a part of this jury, I have the duty, the obligation, to see at least 15 films and talk about them with other filmmakers! And not just any old 15 films, but the 15 films in Competition, drawn from films made all over the world by all sorts of extraordinary filmmakers! And to do this in a city that plays host to one of the most formidable film cultures in the world! Can life ever get much better than this?”

De Heer’s appointment aligns nicely with Tokyo’s 2026 Australia Spotlight, a special showcase within the festival’s World Focus section presented in cooperation with the Australian Embassy in Japan. The strand will include a screening of de Heer’s 2022 feature The Survival of Kindness, which competed at the Berlin International Film Festival and later won the FIPRESCI Prize there.

articles.title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexual assault
articles.summary: Assault survivor Miriam Haley said the "devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away".
body: Disgraced Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison, after a jury found him guilty last year of committing a criminal sexual act against a former assistant.
Appearing in court in a wheelchair, Weinstein denied the allegations but apologised to "anyone I may have hurt by my actions".
Weinstein has already spent several years jailed in New York, where he has faced three trials over rape and abuse allegations. He was convicted in a seperate sex-crime case in Los Angeles.

This is the second time he has been given a prison sentence in the Miriam Haley case. Weinstein was first convicted and sentenced in 2020, but New York's highest court overturned the conviction in 2024, along with another involving actress Jessica Mann. The court ruled that Weinstein did not get a fair trial.
points: Assault survivor Miriam Haley said the "devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away".
